doc.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010

title: Rock and roll behavior and Jimi Hendrix
summary: Prompted by his earlier remark, he criticizes rock musicians trashing hotel rooms and names rock artists he loved.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: You had a statement yesterday, actually just to follow-up on rock & roll, do you have an issue with the way people behave?

Oh, that’s right. You know I don’t know why I said that but it’s true. You know it used to make me mad. You know, these little old Puerto Rican ladies who had to clean up this mess that these guys I mean they didn’t have to break bottles. I mean I party too — oh it’s my phone, where is my phone.
That’s all right, we can edit this tape.
You know what, I’m not going to even answer it. I don’t know who that is. I’ll shut it off.
I’ll bet I know who it was. We were talking about rock & roll, it was probably Eric Clapton calling you “Ralph, what are you doing next week?”
Okay. So we were talking about rock & roll, and the behavior that sometimes is associated with that music.

And I guess I just — would you appreciate it? If your mother had to clean up? I mean because I spent a lot of time in hotel rooms. And I’m not saying, I mean I party but I don’t break glass and I just think these guys — it’s disrespectful. And sometimes the

music sounds that way to me. Not everybody. I mean I love Jimi Hendrix, you know, I loved a lot of people when I was growing up especially, that had something to say. You know? And I’m not against that, not at all. I love James Taylor, I mean that’s not rock & roll, but you know. Who was the other — Laura Nyro, Carole King, yeah, and Jimi Hendrix. I loved Jimi Hendrix. But I didn’t like Cream that much. But I liked Jimi Hendrix you know what I mean?
You don’t have to like everybody I guess.
